claims.text: The applicable material is a multicomponent high-entropy alloy in high-temperature solid and liquid states.
Machine-learning algorithms are the single intervention proposed to overcome current limitations in determining high-temperature thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The machine-learning models will predict properties from alloy composition and crystal structure.
Alloy composition affects the phase or crystal structure stabilized by a high-entropy alloy.
Composition and crystal structure determine or predict melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, melting volume change, and liquid thermodynamic properties.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn relationships between composition, crystal structure, and the listed thermodynamic properties.
Training on data from multiple high-entropy alloys will enable predictions across a large compositional space.
Current computational methods for high-entropy alloys face scalability, computational-cost, and model limitations.
Experimental finite-temperature data for high-entropy alloys are incomplete.
Machine learning will improve the accuracy of the listed property determinations relative to current experimental and computational methods.
Machine learning will improve the availability of the listed property determinations across a large compositional space.
Machine learning will improve the efficiency of the listed property determinations relative to current methods.
The proposed method applies broadly to various high-entropy-alloy compositions in their high-temperature solid and liquid states.
Prediction performance depends on training-data quality and quantity and on the selected machine-learning algorithm.
Failure to predict the measured properties within 10% of experimental values would falsify the hypothesis.
